+# Building & Installing the Droid APK
+
+The Droid APK is a **remote controller** for the Droid backend. The automation
+itself runs on the machine hosting the Node server (desktop via PyAutoGUI,
+Android devices via ADB); the phone app is the control surface — live screen,
+HUD buttons, AI planning, sequences.
+
+## What you need
+
+- The Droid backend running and reachable from the phone
+  (`npm run build && npm start`, default port 3000).
+- Node 20+ and the Android SDK (via Android Studio), **or** just Android
+  Studio to open `android/` and build from the GUI.
+- Java 17 (required by the Android Gradle plugin).
+
+## 1. Start the backend (on your PC / server)
+
+```bash
+npm install
+npm run build
+npm start
+```
+
+Note the machine's LAN IP, e.g. `http://192.168.1.50:3000`.
+The phone must be on the same network (Wi-Fi).
+
+## 2. Sync the web UI into the Android project
+
+```bash
+npm run mobile:sync
+```
+
+This builds the React client into `dist/spa` and copies it into
+`android/app/src/main/assets/public`.
+
+## 3. Build the APK
+
+Option A — Android Studio: open the `android/` folder, wait for Gradle sync,
+then **Build → Build App Bundle(s) / APK(s) → Build APK(s)**.
+
+Option B — command line (needs `ANDROID_HOME` set):
+
+```bash
+cd android
+./gradlew assembleDebug
+```
+
+> **Note:** the binary `gradle-wrapper.jar` is intentionally not committed.
+> If `./gradlew` complains about a missing wrapper jar, fetch it with:
+> ```bash
+> curl -L -o gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar \
+>   https://github.com/gradle/gradle/raw/master/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar
+> ```
body:
These instructions tell users to download the executable gradle-wrapper.jar from a mutable master branch ref with no checksum or signature verification, and that jar is then executed by ./gradlew with full build privileges. A compromised/retargeted upstream ref or a MITM-capable redirect would result in arbitrary code execution on the developer's machine. Prefer committing the wrapper jar (or regenerating it with gradle wrapper from a verified Gradle distribution) and pin to an immutable tag/commit plus a published SHA-256 that is verified before use. ---

Update docs/BUILD_APK.md to remove the insecure “download wrapper jar from master” instruction and replace it with a safer recovery path:

  • Prefer regenerating wrapper artifacts via local Gradle/Android Studio (gradle wrapper) rather than downloading an executable jar directly.
  • If a direct download fallback is retained, pin to an immutable Gradle versioned URL and require SHA-256 verification before use.
  • Keep existing functionality (help users recover missing wrapper jar) while eliminating mutable-ref/no-verification guidance.

Concretely, replace lines 48–54 note block with a secure note that:

  • says wrapper JAR should be committed (or regenerated),
  • provides gradle wrapper command,
  • optional fallback with fixed version URL and sha256sum -c.
